<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed JwtVerifier expiration boundary to reject tokens at the exact instant</title>
  <subtitle>JwtVerifier now rejects tokens whose expiration equals the current instant, closing an off-by-one at the boundary.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>JwtVerifier previously used `claims.getExpiration().before(now)`, which returned false when expiration exactly equaled the current instant, accepting an already-expired token.</fact>
    <fact>The condition is now `claims.getExpiration().isBefore(now) || claims.getExpiration().isEqual(now)`, rejecting the token at the exact boundary.</fact>
    <fact>JwtVerifierTest#expiredAtExactBoundary passes with the fix.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>JwtVerifier had a boundary-condition bug in its expiration check. The original expression `claims.getExpiration().before(now)` uses `Date.before`, which is strictly less-than: a token whose `exp` claim equals the current instant returned false and was therefore treated as still valid. The fix replaces it with `claims.getExpiration().isBefore(now) || claims.getExpiration().isEqual(now)` so that a token expiring exactly at the current instant is rejected. A regression test, `JwtVerifierTest#expiredAtExactBoundary`, pins this behavior and passes. This is a classic expiration-boundary trap: any check must treat equality as expired, not valid.</narrative>
